"P-K-Y look East; M looks West." Decode: Puducherry and Karaikal (East coast, inside Tamil Nadu), Yanam (East coast, inside Andhra Pradesh), Mahe (West coast, Arabian Sea, inside Kerala). UT formed 1962; Chandernagore 1949, Pondicherry 1954. Why it sticks: Mahe's Malayali (Kerala) link makes it the odd one out on the West coast. Teacher: Ink on slide 21. "East" is underlined in the first three rows (Puducherry, Karaikal, Yanam), and a bracket closes after Mahe. So three districts are on the East coast and Mahe is the odd one out (West coast, Arabian Sea). An empty V-shaped peninsula is drawn under the table; nothing is marked on it. Pondicherry's occupation history (mnemonic PDa-FDu-BFBF to India). Pondicherry is synonymous with the French, but they were not the first there: Portuguese (16th century) → Danes (briefly in 1624) → French (1674) → Dutch (captured briefly in 1693) → British. The English captured Pondicherry in 1761 and restored it to the French via the Treaty of Paris (1763); the British captured it again (for example in 1793) before finally returning it to the French in 1814. It remained French until transferred to India in 1954. Mnemonic: Pass Dosa For Dad, Bro! P-D-F-D-B: who held Pondicherry, in order. Decode: Portuguese (16th century), Danes (1624), French (1674), Dutch (1693), British (1761, again 1793, back to the French in 1814); India 1954. The SECOND was the Danes, not the French. Why it sticks: Prelims 2010: answer (a) Only 1 (the chapter's ruling, over the board's tick on (d)); "occupied" counts even a very temporary occupation. West coast: Surat, Daman, Bassein, Bombay, Goa, Cannanore, Mahe, Calicut, Cochin, Cape Comorin; east coast: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Madras, Pondicherry, Karikal, Tranquebar, Negapatam, Hugli, Chinsura, Chandernagore, Calcutta, Balasore; Sri Lanka marked.

items.t: 20 · Who came when: a master comparison
items.x: Company   Founded   First factory in India   Nature   Fate Portuguese (Estado da India)   Voyages from 1498   Calicut 1500 (destroyed); Cochin 1500 (permanent); Fort Manuel 1503   State enterprise (Crown is the trader)   Decline; Goa, Daman, Diu held to 1961 Dutch VOC   1602   Masulipatnam 1605; Fort Geldria, Pulicat 1610   Joint-stock company; world's first   Colachel 1741, Bedara 1759, Kew Letters 1795; dissolved 1799 English EIC   31 Dec 1600   Masulipatnam 1611 (temporary); Surat 1613 (permanent)   Joint-stock (4th in England); monopoly by Charter   Became the ruling power; Crown rule later Danish EIC   1616   Tranquebar 1620 (Fort Dansborg)   Weak Charter company (12-year monopoly)   Mainland settlements sold to Britain by 1845; Nicobars 1868 French EIC   1664   Surat 1668   Private at first, later nationalised (PSU)   Pondicherry to India in 1954 Two orders for "who came first." The Lecture 12 board (PYQ 6, slide 32) writes Portugal 1500 -> EIC 1600 -> Dutch 1602 -> Danes 1616 -> French, which is the order of company founding (the EIC's 1600 Charter comes before the VOC's 1602). The answer slide (slide 33) and Table T1 to T5 give the order of first factory in India: Portuguese 1498-1500, Dutch 1605, English 1611, Danish 1620, French 1664/1668. Use the order of the handout's tables (first factory) unless the question says "company founded"; for the last to arrive, the French win either way. Mnemonic: Charter says E-D, Factory says D-E. "Founding: English before Dutch. First factory: Dutch before English." Decode: Founding order = Portugal 1500, EIC 1600, VOC 1602, Danes 1616, French. First-factory order (use unless the question says "founded") = Portuguese 1498-1500, Dutch 1605, English 1611, Danish 1620, French 1664/1668. Why it sticks: the English and Dutch swap places between the two lists; the French stay last in both (Prelims 2007: answer French).

items.t: 21 · Chapter 8 PYQs discussed in class (Lecture 12)
items.x: Source: Lecture 12, slides 22 to 55. Each PYQ has a question slide with the teacher's marks (T and F, ticks, crosses) and then an answer slide. There are 16 questions. The numbers (PYQ 1 to 16) are as printed on the slides; the slide order is not numeric (13, 15 and 16 come before 10, 11, 12 and 14). Rule used here: only what the slides and the teacher's ink show.   Slides   PYQ and year   What was asked   Answer   Teacher's marks and trap    --- --- --- --- ---    22-23   PYQ 1, Prelims 1995   Who used Hughly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal   (a) the Portuguese   Carnatic over Tranquebar, Bengal over Serampore     24-25   PYQ 2, Prelims 2003   Which statement is NOT correct on European entry   (a): Goa was taken in 1510, not 1499   T circled after (d); "09-K" on the answer slide     26-27   PYQ 3, Prelims 2005   Which statement on modern Kochi is correct   (b): the Dutch defeated the Portuguese and built forts (1663)   (a) "1795 x presence" F; (b) T; (c) F; (d) F     28-29   PYQ 4, Prelims 2006   Where the EIC got permission for a factory in 1613   (d) Surat   No ink     30-31   PYQ 5, Prelims 2007   The first fort constructed by the British in India   (b) Fort St George   "constructed" underlined; tick on (b); S, M, B, C sketch     32-33   PYQ 6, Prelims 2007   The last Europeans to come as traders   (c) the French   Tick on French; chain Portugal to Danes to Fr     34-35   PYQ 7, Prelims 2010   Pondicherry: first, second, English   (a) Only 1 (slide answer)   Board ticks (d); conflict, see the alert     36-37   PYQ 8, Prelims 2012   What the English introduced for the first time   (d) None of these   "1st Time," "English" underlined; Babur 26-30; Portugal     38-39   PYQ 9, Prelims 2015   EIC factories in the first quarter of the 17th century   (a) Only 1 (Broach)   "1600-1625"; Surat 1613, Masulipatnam 1611, Madras 1639     40-41   PYQ 13, Prelims 2021   Repeat of Prelims 2015   (a) 1 only   No ink     42-43   PYQ 15, Prelims 2023   Which Gujarat ruler surrendered Diu   (c) Bahadur Shah   "BOMBAY 1534"     44-45   PYQ 16, Prelims 2025   How many of papaya, pineapple, guava the Portuguese introduced   (c) All the three   No ink     46-47   PYQ 10, Prelims 2018   Staple Bengal exports in the mid-18th century   (d) cotton, silk, saltpetre, opium   "raw" underlined, F on (a); "1750s"; Gunpowder     48-49   PYQ 11, Prelims 2019   Plants domesticated in the New World   (a) tobacco, cocoa, rubber   "American"; T on (a); F on the rest     50-52   PYQ 12, Prelims 2021   St Francis Xavier   (c) 1 and 3   Statement 2 circled, "False"; tick on (c)     53-55   PYQ 14, Prelims 2022   Gajapati / Albuquerque 09-15 / Madras   (b) 2 and 3 only   "Gajapati" circled; (b) ticked; (a), (c) crossed   PYQ 1 · Prelims 1995: Hughly piracy (slides 22 and 23) Answer: (a) the Portuguese. They misused their trade privileges from their Bengal base: piracy and the slave trade. This is why Shah Jahan ordered his Bengal governor Qasim Khan to eject them from Hugli in 1631-32 (see section 11). Wrong options: (b) the French at Chandernagore were trading, not pirate dens; (c) the Danish bases (Tranquebar, Serampore) were lawful; (d) the British entered Bengal at Hugli in 1651, after the piracy was suppressed. Teacher: On the answer slide he wrote "Carnatic" above Tranquebar and "Bengal" above Serampore, each with a short stroke pointing to the name: the two Danish bases are in different regions (Tranquebar in the Carnatic, Serampore in Bengal). The question slide has no ink. Mnemonic: Portuguese Pirates at Hugli. "P for Pirates, P for Portuguese." Decode: Prelims 1995 answer (a): the Portuguese misused trade privileges for piracy and the slave trade at Hugli; Shah Jahan 27-58 had his Bengal governor Qasim Khan eject them in 1631-32. British came to Hugli later, in 1651. Why it sticks: French (Chandernagore) and Danes (Tranquebar, Serampore) were just trading.  PYQ 1, Prelims 1995 answer slide: the Portuguese used Hughly for piracy. Teacher's ink: Carnatic over Tranquebar, Bengal over Serampore. PYQ 2 · Prelims 2003: European entry, the NOT-correct statement (slides 24 and 25) Answer: (a) is the wrong statement: Albuquerque 09-15 captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510, not 1499. Da Gama reached Calicut in 1498 and merely traded. (b), (c), (d) are correct: Masulipatnam (1611); Balasore and Hariharpur, Orissa (1633); Dupleix 42-54 took Madras in 1746 (1st Carnatic War). Teacher: On the question slide a circled T stands after option (d) (a true statement; the question asks for the false one). On the answer slide "09-K" is written after "1498 and merely traded" (hard to read; it sits where Albuquerque 09-15 belongs, so it is probably his reign). Mnemonic: Goa 15-10 inside 09-15. "Albuquerque 09-15 took Goa in fifteen-ten, not fourteen-ninety-nine." Decode: Prelims 2003 NOT-correct statement is (a): Goa was taken in 1510 (from Bijapur), not 1499; Da Gama reached Calicut in 1498 and only traded. Why it sticks: 1510 sits right inside the 09-15 span, one year after he starts. PYQ 3 · Prelims 2005: modern Kochi (slides 26 and 27) Answer: (b). The Dutch captured Cochin from the Portuguese in 1663 and held it as their key South-India base. Why the others are wrong: (a) Cochin was under British rule 1795-1947, not Dutch till independence; (c) the order is reversed (Portuguese 1500 first, Dutch 1663 second); (d) Cochin did become part of British India after 1795. Teacher: (a) "1795 x presence" (no Dutch presence after 1795), circled F. (b) "built forts" underlined, "1663," circled T. (c) circled F. (d) circled F. The Kew Letters (1795, section 14) are why the British, not the Dutch, held Cochin after 1795.  PYQ 3, Prelims 2005, modern Kochi: teacher's marks. (a) 1795 no presence, F; (b) built forts underlined, 1663, T; (c) F; (d) F. PYQ 4 · Prelims 2006: the 1613 factory (slides 28 and 29) Answer: (d) Surat. Jahangir 05-27 issued a Royal Farman in 1613 giving the right to a permanent factory at Surat, after the Battle of Swally (1612). Wrong options: (a) Bangalore came only after the Anglo-Mysore Wars; (b) Madras was acquired in 1639; (c) Masulipatnam had a temporary factory (1611), but the 1613 farman was for Surat. No teacher ink. This is the 1612 versus 1613 point in section 10. PYQ 5 · Prelims 2007: the first British fort (slides 30 and 31) Answer: (b) Fort St George. Madras, built 1639-44: the first fort built by the EIC in India. Wrong options: (a) Fort William (Calcutta) was built 1696-1700; (c) Fort St David (Cuddalore) was purchased in 1690, not built; (d) Fort St Angelo (Kannur) was built by the Portuguese in 1505. Teacher: "constructed" is underlined (the trap word: St David was bought, not built). Side labels: (a) CAL, (b) MAD (underlined), (c) MAD, (d) "?"; a tick on (b). Sketch: "S, M, B, C" over a line, with SURAT, MADRAS, Bo (Bombay) and CALCUTTA hanging below it: the order of the EIC's main centres: Surat, Madras, Bombay, Calcutta (matches the slide 9 board in section 16). Mnemonic: George Grew it, David Dealt for it. "Built = George. Bought = David." Decode: Prelims 2007, underline "constructed": Fort St George (Madras, built 1639-44) is the first fort built by the EIC. Fort St David (Cuddalore) was purchased in 1690; Fort William (Calcutta) was built later, 1696-1700; Fort St Angelo (Kannur) is Portuguese, 1505. Why it sticks: St David was a deal, so it fails the word "constructed".  PYQ 5, Prelims 2007, first British fort: constructed underlined; CAL, MAD, MAD labels; tick on Fort St George; S, M, B, C sketch for Surat, Madras, Bombay, Calcutta. PYQ 6 · Prelims 2007: the last Europeans to come (slides 32 and 33) Answer: (c) the French. The French EIC was founded in 1664 and set up its first Indian factory at Surat in 1668, the latest of the four. Chronology on the answer slide: Portuguese 1498 -> Dutch 1605 -> English 1611 -> Danish 1620 -> French 1664/1668. Teacher: A tick beside French (underlined). Board chain: "PORTUGAL (1500) -> EIC (1600) -> DUTCH 1602," then an arrow down to "Danes 1616," then an arrow to "Fr" (left unfinished). See the alert at the end of section 20 on the two orders (company founding versus first factory).  PYQ 6, Prelims 2007, last Europeans to come: tick on French; board chain Portugal 1500, EIC 1600, Dutch 1602, Danes 1616, then Fr. PYQ 7 · Prelims 2010: Pondicherry (slides 34 and 35) Question: (1) the first European power to occupy it was the Portuguese; (2) the second was the French; (3) the English never occupied it. Options: (a) Only 1; (b) 2 and 3; (c) Only 3; (d) 1, 2 and 3. Answer slide: (a) Only 1. Sequence: Portuguese -> Danes (1624) -> French (1674) -> Dutch (1693) -> English (1761/1793/1814) -> India (1954). Statement 2 is wrong (the second were the Danes; the French were fourth). Statement 3 is wrong (the English captured it several times and restored it by treaty). Teacher: Board marks: circled T after (1), circled F after (2), circled T after (3), a tick beside (d), and a boxed starred note: "WORD "occupied" = VERY TEMPORARY OCCUPATION ALSO" (WORD and ALSO underlined). A small "L" under (a) is unclear. The board and the answer slide disagree. The board ticks (d) and puts T on statement 3; the answer slide gives (a) Only 1 and the handout's occupation sequence (section 19 alert: Portuguese, Danes, French, Dutch, British) also makes statements 2 and 3 false. The teacher's own word-note, that "occupied" counts even a very temporary occupation, means the English did occupy it (1761, 1793), so statement 3 is false. Use (a) Only 1 (handout and slide answer); treat the board tick on (d) as unresolved and check the class recording.  PYQ 7, Prelims 2010, Pondicherry: teacher's marks T, F, T, tick on (d), and the boxed note WORD occupied = very temporary occupation also. The answer slide gives (a) Only 1. PYQ 8 · Prelims 2012: what the English introduced (slides 36 and 37) Answer: (d) None of these. (1) Soil-and-crop revenue assessment existed in medieval India (Sher Shah 40-45, Todar Mal); (2) mobile cannons came with Babur 26-30 at Panipat (1526); (3) tobacco and red chillies were introduced by the Portuguese. Teacher: "introduced" is underlined with "1st Time" above it, and "English" is underlined: the question asks what the English brought for the first time. A circled F sits above the question near (1) and another at the far right edge (the board marks the first two statements false). Under (a): an arrow from the cannons to "Babur 26-30" (underlined) and an arrow to "PORTUGAL" for tobacco and red chillies. Tick on (d). Mnemonic: "Sab Pehle": all were earlier. S-B-P = Sher Shah 40-45, Babur 26-30, Portugal. Decode: Prelims 2012 asked what the English introduced "for the first time": revenue assessment goes to Sher Shah 40-45 (and Todar Mal); mobile cannons to Babur 26-30 (Panipat 1526); tobacco and red chillies to the Portuguese. Answer (d) None. Why it sticks: Hindi "sab pehle" = everything came earlier, so the English introduced nothing first.  PYQ 8, Prelims 2012, English introductions: introduced (1st Time) and English underlined; circled F marks; Babur 26-30 for mobile cannons; Portugal for tobacco and red chillies; tick on None of these. PYQ 9 and PYQ 13 · Prelims 2015 and its repeat in Prelims 2021 (slides 38 to 41) Question (both years): in the first quarter of the 17th century, EIC factories were at (1) Broach, (2) Chicacole, (3) Trichinopoly. Answer: (a) Only 1. Only Broach (Bharuch) had an EIC factory then: the Roe-era (1616-19) factories were Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach, all in the Mughal Empire. Chicacole (Srikakulam) and Trichinopoly had none; early South-India trade centred on Masulipatnam. Teacher: "1600-1625" above the question; an arrow from "ENGLISH" to "factories" (underlined); a stroke over Broach. Map sketch: the Gujarat circle with "SURAT 1613," and on the east coast "Masulipatnam 1611" and "MADRAS 1639." A second small sketch shows BROACH and SURAT. Reason: by 1625 the EIC was only on the Gujarat side and at Masulipatnam; Madras came in 1639, after the quarter ended. PYQ 13 (Prelims 2021) is the same question and the same answer, with no ink: UPSC repeated it. Mnemonic: Quarter-century clock: "bas Bharuch". Window = 1600-1625; only Broach (Bharuch) fits. Decode: Roe-era factories 1616-19 were Agra, Ahmedabad, Broach. Surat 1613 and Masulipatnam 1611 are inside the window; Madras 1639 misses it. Chicacole and Trichinopoly had no EIC factory. Prelims 2015 and 2021: answer (a) Only 1. Why it sticks: bas = only; one answer, one town.  PYQ 9, Prelims 2015, first-quarter 17C factories: 1600-1625; English factories; map sketch with Surat 1613, Masulipatnam 1611, Madras 1639; Broach and Surat sketch. PYQ 15 · Prelims 2023: who surrendered Diu (slides 42 and 43) Answer: (c) Bahadur Shah. Under Nuno da Cunha 29-38 the Portuguese acquired Bassein (1534) and Diu (1535) from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat. Wrong options: (a) Ahmad Shah (1411-42, as printed on the slide) did not surrender Diu; (b) Mahmud Begarha resisted the Portuguese; (d) Muhammad Shah 19-48 was a later, minor ruler. Teacher: "BOMBAY 1534" is written at the right of the answer line: Bombay passed to the Portuguese with the 1534 Bassein deal (the "1534-1661: Portugal" note in section 17.2). The question slide has no ink. PYQ 16 · Prelims 2025: Portuguese fruits (slides 44 and 45) Answer: (c) All the three. The Portuguese brought tobacco, red chillies, papaya, pineapple and guava from the New World (section 4.7). No teacher ink. PYQ 10 · Prelims 2018: Bengal exports (slides 46 and 47) Answer: (d) cotton, silk, saltpetre and opium: the textile, saltpetre and opium mix that fuelled EIC profits before and after Plassey. Teacher: "1750s" (top right) with "L Textiles." A circled F on (a) with "raw" underlined: India exported finished goods, not raw cotton. Beside (a): "Before IR (1750-1850)" and, underlined, "FG of India" (the first letters are hard to read; it reads like "finished goods of India," as in the Lecture 10 board). On (d): cotton, saltpetre and opium underlined, and under saltpetre "L Gunpowder." Tick on (d). Mnemonic: Bengal sends C-S-S-O, never "raw". "Cotton cloth, Silk, Saltpetre, Opium." Decode: Prelims 2018 answer (d): cotton, silk, saltpetre (for gunpowder) and opium, the 1750s mix. India exported finished goods, so any option saying "raw" cotton is false (teacher's F on (a)). Why it sticks: "raw" is the red-flag word; saltpetre goes bang.  PYQ 10, Prelims 2018, Bengal exports: 1750s textiles; raw underlined and F on (a); Before IR (1750-1850) FG of India; tick on (d) with cotton, saltpetre (gunpowder) and opium underlined. PYQ 11 · Prelims 2019: New-World plants (slides 48 and 49) Answer: (a) tobacco, cocoa and rubber. The Portuguese brought tobacco, red chillies, papaya, pineapple and guava to India; the fuller list is in the Geography notes. Teacher: "American" above the question; circled T on (a); F on (b), (c) and (d). Under cotton in (b): "Bengal" with an arrow, and "Cotton" underlined in (c): cotton is the Old-World (Bengal) crop, so it cannot be an American plant. Do not mix two lists. This PYQ asks which plants were domesticated in the New World (tobacco, cocoa, rubber qualify). Section 4.7 lists what the Portuguese brought to India: cocoa and rubber are not on that list (they reached India in the British period). The handout and this slide agree; the questions are different. Mnemonic: Only Tobacco travels in both lists. Two lists, one overlap. Decode: New-World set in Prelims 2019 answer (a) = tobacco, cocoa, rubber. Portuguese gifts = tobacco, red chillies, papaya, pineapple, guava. Overlap = tobacco; cocoa and rubber came in the British period. Cotton is the Old-World (Bengal) crop, so it is never an American plant. Why it sticks: read the question's verb: "domesticated in the New World" versus "brought by the Portuguese".  PYQ 11, Prelims 2019, New-World plants: American written above; circled T on (a); F on (b), (c), (d); Bengal under cotton; Cotton underlined in (c). PYQ 12 · Prelims 2021: St Francis Xavier (slides 50 to 52) Answer: (c) 1 and 3. Xavier was a founding member of the Jesuit Order (1, true) and the Feast of St Francis Xavier is celebrated in Goa each year (3, true). Statement 2 is the trap: he did not die in Goa; he died on Shangchuan Island (off China) in 1552. His remains were brought to Goa (Basilica of Bom Jesus), but death is not burial. Slide 52 calls it a signature trap: UPSC tested death versus burial. Teacher: Statement (2) is circled and "False" is written above it. F beside (a), (b) and (d); a tick on (c). (Same point as section 4.6.)  PYQ 12, Prelims 2021, St Francis Xavier: statement 2 circled with False above; F beside (a), (b), (d); tick on (c). PYQ 14 · Prelims 2022: Gajapati, Albuquerque 09-15, Madras (slides 53 to 55) Question: (1) Dutch factories on lands granted by the Gajapati; (2) Albuquerque 09-15 captured Goa; (3) English factory at Madras leased from Vijayanagara. Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. Statement 2: Albuquerque 09-15 took Goa from Bijapur in 1510. Statement 3: the EIC got Madraspatanam in 1639 from the Hindu Nayakas (Vijayanagara governors). Statement 1 is the trap: the Dutch did not get land from the Gajapati dynasty, a 15th-century Odisha dynasty that had declined well before the Dutch came (1605 onwards). Do not confuse later Odisha-coast rulers with the Gajapatis themselves. Teacher: "Gajapati" circled with a large loop. "09-15" above Albuquerque 09-15, a circled T and "1510"; "1639" (underlined) below statement 2 for Madras; "1336-1646" under Vijayanagara. (a) and (c) crossed out, (b) ticked. The question says Madras was "leased" from Vijayanagara; the handout says the EIC purchased the Madraspatanam land from the Hindu Nayakas (section 17.1). Learn "purchased" (handout wins); the answer slide still counts statement 3 as correct. Mnemonic: The Gajapati elephant is long gone. "Gaja (elephant) of the 15th century cannot give land to 1605 Dutch." Decode: Prelims 2022 answer (b) 2 and 3: (2) Albuquerque 09-15 took Goa in 1510 (true); (3) Madraspatanam from the Hindu Nayakas in 1639, Vijayanagara 1336-1646 (true, "purchased" in the handout); (1) Dutch land from the Gajapati dynasty of Odisha is false, since the dynasty had declined long before the Dutch (1605 onwards). Why it sticks: "2 + 3 = B"; statement 1 is the elephant that no longer exists.  PYQ 14, Prelims 2022, Gajapati, Albuquerque, Madras: Gajapati circled; Albuquerque 09-15, T, 1510; 1639; Vijayanagara 1336-1646; (a) and (c) crossed, (b) ticked.

items.t: Memory hooks: chapter in one breath
items.x: Mnemonic: The whole chapter as one voyage. Story: "Ottomans lock the road (1453); the Pope splits the sea (1494); Gama knocks at Calicut (1498); Cabral builds at Cochin (1500) and Albuquerque 09-15 walls it (1503). Almeida 05-09 wins the sea at Diu (1509), Albuquerque 09-15 grabs Goa (1510), Nuno da Cunha 29-38 makes it the capital (1530). Then the Armada falls (1588), the English (1600) and Dutch (1602) charters sail in, Best wins at Swally (1612) so Jahangir 05-27 signs Surat (1613), and the Danes tag along (1616). Roe gets liberal rights (1618), the Presidencies rise S-M-B-C, and the Charter of 1661 turns the Company into a State. The French last of all at Pondicherry (1674)." Decode: 1453 Ottoman blockade; 1494 Tordesillas; 1498 Calicut; 1500 Cochin factory; 1503 Fort Manuel; 1509 Diu; 1510 Goa; 1530 capital to Goa; 1588 Armada; 1600 EIC; 1602 VOC; 1612 Swally; 1613 Surat farman; 1616 Danes; 1618 Roe's farman and Surat Presidency; Presidencies Surat, Madras, Bombay, Calcutta; 1661 Charles II 60-85's Charter; 1674 Pondicherry. Why it sticks: one breath, one direction: from Europe's closed road to the Company that became a State.

items.t: Exam lens: priority and PYQs
items.x: Chapter 9 title slide: Carnatic Wars (1746-63), Modern Indian History. Teacher's ink at the top right, inside a big bracket: "# NOT many questions FROM WARS in PRELIMS", with a fork under WARS to "EIC (vs) Indian Kingdom" (vs circled); "# Recently 1 Mains PYQ". Below the bracket: "# Conceptual VERY interesting, imp" (VERY underlined, two small ticks under it, "imp" written below). Teacher: Priority marking on the title slide. (1) "Not many questions from WARS in Prelims": by wars the teacher means EIC versus Indian kingdom wars. (2) "Recently 1 Mains PYQ." (3) "Conceptual: VERY interesting, imp" (VERY underlined and ticked). The reasoning: the battles themselves are rarely asked, so do not mug up battle trivia. Read this chapter for the concept: how a trading company built an empire, and the model that Dupleix 42-54 invented.   Year and paper   What was asked   The answer or trap   Where in this chapter    --- --- --- ---    Prelims 1995 (Lecture 13, slides 23 and 24)   Which pair is correctly matched? (a) Battle of Buxar: Mir Jafar 57-60 vs Clive 57-67; (b) Battle of Wandiwash: French vs East India Company; (c) Battle of Chilianwala: Dalhousie 48-56 vs Marathas; (d) Battle of Kharda: Nizam vs East India Company   (b). Wandiwash (1760) = French vs the EIC, the decisive battle of the 3rd Carnatic War; the British under Eyre Coote beat the French under Count de Lally. Traps: Buxar (1764) = EIC vs Mir Qasim 60-63 (with Awadh and Shah Alam II 60-06), not Mir Jafar 57-60; Chilianwala (1849) = EIC under Dalhousie 48-56 vs the Sikhs (2nd Anglo-Sikh War); Kharda (1795) = Nizam vs the Marathas   Section 6.2     Prelims 1996 (Lecture 13, slides 25 and 26)   Who were the first European to initiate the policy of taking part in the quarrels of Indian princes with a view to acquire territories? (a) Clive 57-67 (b) Dupleix 42-54 (c) Albuquerque 09-15 (d) Warren Hastings 73-85   (b) Dupleix 42-54. He invented the model of empire building in the 2nd Carnatic War (backing Muzaffar Jung 50-51 and Chanda Sahib 49-52). Clive 57-67 and Warren Hastings 73-85 used and refined the model; Albuquerque 09-15 belongs to an earlier era of direct conquest (Goa 1510)   Section 5.1     Mains (teacher's board, Lecture 13, slide 9)   "Model of empire building (in India) by trading companies was founded by the French and implemented by the British. Analyse."   Founded by French = the 2nd Carnatic War (Dupleix 42-54's four steps). Implemented by British = future topics (Plassey, Subsidiary Alliance)   Section 5.1 (the model) and Section 6.5   Teacher: How the teacher solved Prelims 1995 on the slide: a circled F against (a); a tick on (b); in (c) he struck out "Marathas" and wrote SIKH, circled F; in (d) he struck out "East India Company" and wrote MARATHAS 1795, circled F. The handout's alert says the same: UPSC asked "match the battle to who fought it" by jumbling correct pairs. So learn each battle as a pair: battle + the two sides. Teacher: How the teacher solved Prelims 1996: he underlined "first European", "quarrels of Indian princes" and "to acquire territories" and then wrote each option's years beside it: Clive 57-67: "57-60, 65-67" [1700s, Governor Bengal Presidency]; Dupleix 42-54 [1742-54]; Albuquerque 09-15; Warren Hastings 73-85 [1700s]. The reasoning: place the four men on the timeline. Albuquerque 09-15 is 16th century and conquered directly; of the three 18th-century men, Dupleix 42-54 comes first, so the others can only be copying him. Three small checks on the PYQ slides. (1) Beside Albuquerque 09-15 the teacher's bracket reads "[1509-1615]" as written; Chapter 8 gives his governorship as 1509-15, so treat the "16" as a slip and check your own notebook. (2) The answer slide calls Warren Hastings 73-85 a "later EIC Governor-General (1772-85)" while the teacher's ink writes 73-85. (3) The board question on slide 9 is headed "FYQ-M" [unclear: probably PYQ-M, Mains]; its year is not written. What to prepare: Prelims hooks: battle and sides pairs (Adyar 1746, Ambur 1749, Arcot 1751, Wandiwash 1760, plus Buxar, Kharda and Chilianwala from the 1995 question); the three treaties in order (Aix-La-Chapelle 1748, Pondicherry 1754, Paris 1763); Dupleix 42-54 = first European to interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes; the five French posts (PM KYC); Hyderabad = first Subsidiary Alliance (1798); the 1661 Charter powers. Mains hooks: how a trading company became a State (wars for trade versus wars for territory); Dupleix 42-54's four-step model, founded by the French and implemented by the British; why Adyar 1746 was a turning point; why the French lost and the EIC won; how the Carnatic Wars led to Plassey and to British domination of South India.

Sections 1 and 2 give the frame (the Charter of 1661, wars for trade versus wars for territory, the Anglo-Mughal War). Sections 3 to 6 are the three Carnatic Wars. The teacher's short codes on the board: CW = Carnatic War (1st, 2nd, 3rd); (T) = territory; AWoS = Austrian War of Succession; Fr eic and Eng eic = the French and English East India Companies; MJ = Muzaffar Jung 50-51; Hyd = Hyderabad.
